title: 2026-09-11 POC scoping - private networking - NovaHealth Systems
summary: POC scoping focused on private networking and data residency for a HIPAA-adjacent workload. Evaluate VPC peering vs PrivateLink, regional placement (us-east-1 vs eu-west-1), egress constraints, and benchmark success criteria (p99 latency < 150ms for chat, 400 reqs/sec for embeddings). Agree on POC timeline ~3 weeks and required artifacts (AWS account IDs, CIDR ranges, compliance pack).
next_steps: Redwood (Priya) to share compliance/security pack (SOC2, HIPAA notes, KMS integration guide) by 2026-09-15
Customer (Carlos) to provide AWS account IDs, VPC IDs, and preferred CIDR ranges for peering by 2026-09-13
Schedule 2-hour benchmarking window with NovaHealth and Redwood SE for week of 2026-09-20
Redwood to propose POC success criteria and test harness by 2026-09-16
action_items: Priya: prepare benchmark plan + test harness (embedding and chat workloads) - due 2026-09-16
Jordan: send commercial POC template and pricing outline - due 2026-09-14
Carlos: share AWS account numbers, VPC peering contacts, and zg-logging requirements - due 2026-09-13
Lena: confirm internal stakeholders and timeline for a pilot decision - due 2026-09-18
transcript: [00:00] Meeting header: 2026-09-11 15:00 PDT / Duration: 48 minutes
[00:02] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time. quick intros? we have Priya from Redwood SE and I'm Jordan on the AE side.
[00:08] Lena: Hi all, Lena here, VP Eng at NovaHealth. we run clinical decision support and some patient-facing chat, so latency and PHI controls matter.
[00:14] Samir: Samir, security architect. primary concerns: data residency, egress, and proof we can keep PHI off public internet.

[00:22] Priya: Great — goal for today is to align on POC scope: networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region placement, success criteria (latency/throughput), and timeline. we'll also surface what artifacts we need.
[00:41] Carlos: quick note — our infra is in AWS primarily, prod in us-east-1, some data in eu-west-1 for EU customers. we also use KMS with a dedicated CMK.
[00:50] Jordan: perfect. for the POC are you planning to run inference in Redwood Private (VPC peering) or wanted to evaluate both hosted+privatelink?

[00:58] Samir: we prefer private networking so traffic never traverses public internet. open to whichever gives stronger access controls: vpc peering or privatelink. concerned about cross-region egress costs too.

[01:12] Priya: short primer: VPC peering is direct peering (L3), generally lower latency but requires route table changes and non-transitive. PrivateLink exposes an endpoint service (ENI) in the provider VPC — it's easier for segmented networking and avoids routing changes but can add per-GB charges.
[01:35] Lena: what about data residency? we have EU patient data that must remain in eu-west-1. can Redwood guarantee region pinning for the model endpoints during POC?

[01:44] Priya: yes, with Redwood Private you can pin endpoints to regions. for hosted we can route to region-specific clusters; for Dedicated/Private we run in your selected region. during the POC we can stand up in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 as separate tests.
[02:05] Carlos: how do you handle egress constraints — like we can't have responses forwarded to third-party telemetry outside our VPC?

[02:12] Priya: Redwood's Private deployment supports customer-managed egress — you can funnel logs to your endpoints or disable remote telemetry. for hosted we offer VPC peering or PrivateLink options and redact logs upon request; need to share the security pack for specifics.
[02:31] Samir: KMS? we need to control keys for model inputs/outputs at rest.

[02:35] Priya: we support KMS integration and can work with customer CMKs in Private. Hosted has envelope encryption options and dedicated key support on some tiers; again will include details in the security pack.
[02:50] Jordan: let's get specific on success criteria — what would make the POC a win for NovaHealth?

[02:58] Lena: two things: latency for chat (p99) under 150ms for short-context queries (~256 tokens) and embedding throughput of ~400 req/s with 99% success over a 30-minute window. also no PHI leaving the designated region and SOC2/HIPAA checks passed.

[03:20] Priya: solid. we'll map those to benchmark tests. for Chat latency we can run a constant concurrency test and measure p50/p95/p99. for embeddings we'll run a sustained load run. do you have representative prompt sets?
[03:32] Lena: yes, we'll share a redacted prompt set and sample payload sizes — mostly 32-512 token inputs.
[03:40] Carlos: network details — we're running in a private subnet with NAT restricted. we prefer initiating peering from our side. any blockers?

[03:47] Priya: fine; we typically do customer-initiated peering so you create the peering connection and we accept. for PrivateLink we'll ask you to create an interface endpoint in your VPC and then we expose a service. both approaches require CIDR planning.
[04:05] Samir: about IP ranges — we need to ensure no overlap. we'll share our VPC CIDR and EKS pod ranges. what's Redwood's preferred pattern?

[04:12] Priya: send us the VPC CIDR and we can suggest non-overlapping ranges. for peering you'll need to update route tables. for PrivateLink there's no route table change but you do create an ENI which sits in subnets.

[04:29] Jordan: cost tradeoffs quick callout — PrivateLink has data processing fees on top of transfer; peering has data transfer charges at normal AWS rates but lower per-request overhead. we'll include an estimate in the POC doc.
[04:43] Lena: good to know. for auditing we need audit logs and access logs retained for 1 year; can Redwood provide those with S3 export?
[04:52] Priya: yes, audit logs can be exported. in Private we can push logs to your S3, in hosted we can provide a delivery option. we'll list retention/configuration in the security pack.
[05:06] Carlos: on the benchmark harness — do you use synthetic traffic or replay of production traffic?

[05:11] Priya: either. for PHI-sensitive stuff we recommend redacted replay or synthetic that mirrors token distribution. we have a harness that can replay and measure p99 latency, error rates, and tokens/sec.
[05:23] Samir: threat model question — will model weights or prompts ever be stored in Redwood logs? we need guarantees they won't be persisted unencrypted.

[05:30] Priya: by default we don't persist prompts beyond what's needed for debugging; for the POC we can disable request logging and ensure ephemeral retention. full details in the pack, but we support customer-managed KMS and can turn off transcript storage.
[05:46] Jordan: timeline — you mentioned 3-week POC. what's realistic from your side?
[05:51] Lena: if we can get accounts/CIDR by next Monday and a benchmark window scheduled the week after, 3 weeks is comfortable for an evaluation and internal signoff.

[06:00] Priya: proposed plan: week 0 (this week) share docs + networking info; week 1 set up peering/privatelink and stand up endpoints; week 2 run benchmarks and iterate; week 3 review results and decision. adjustable.
[06:18] Carlos: setup details — will Redwood need any IAM roles in our account for peering?

[06:22] Priya: no cross-account role for peering; you'd create the peering and we accept. for Private deployments we may ask for a connector role to push logs or for automated deployments; we'll scope that in the POC runbook.
[06:37] Lena: performance expectations — for embeddings 400 req/sec is token light but concurrency matters. what's your batching behavior?

[06:44] Priya: Redwood runtime uses continuous batching; in Private you can tune batch/window size. we'll provide recommended configs to hit throughput while keeping p99 bounds. SE will run with production-like concurrency in the benchmark.
[07:02] Samir: compliance — do you have HIPAA-specific attestation or BAA?
[07:06] Priya: Redwood has a BAA process for Private and Dedicated customers. hosted customers may need additional controls; we'll include BAA scoping and compliance notes in the security pack.
[07:17] Jordan: can we talk about a minimal benchmark matrix? Priya?

[07:21] Priya: yes: Test A — chat latency: 100 concurrent users, short context (avg 128 tokens), 15-minute run, measure p50/95/99. Success: p99 < 150ms. Test B — embeddings: sustained 400 req/s for 30 minutes, success: <2% errors and throughput sustained. Test C — region residency: requests for EU users handled in eu-west-1 endpoints; verify no egress to us-east-1. we'll collect network traces and logs.
[07:53] Carlos: what auth patterns do you support? SSO, mTLS?

[07:57] Priya: we support API keys, mTLS for PrivateLink, and SAML/SSO for console access. for programmatic traffic you can use short-lived credentials or our Private endpoint plus IAM policies. detail in runbook.
[08:10] Lena: downtime and fallbacks — what happens if an endpoint in eu-west-1 is degraded?

[08:14] Priya: you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model in another region but for PII reasons you might prefer no fallback. we can set policies per-route to avoid cross-region handling. we'll document options.
[08:30] Samir: any sample runbook or network diagram we can look at?
[08:34] Jordan: we'll attach a sample runbook and a template network diagram to the notes. Priya will update with NovaHealth specifics.
[08:41] Carlos: also need to understand S3 egress for log exports — if logs are exported, they must remain in our S3 and not be transferred out.
[08:48] Priya: yep we'll ensure logs are delivered to your S3 in-region and include retention lifecycle options.
[08:55] Lena: any blockers on your side for the peering approach vs PrivateLink?

[09:00] Priya: both doable. peering gives slightly lower overhead and latency; PrivateLink is operationally simpler for segmented networks. choice depends on your ops preferences and cost sensitivity.
[09:12] Jordan: quick note — we'll include a cost estimate comparing expected egress fees + PrivateLink per-GB costs vs peering transfer rates for your projected traffic volumes.
[09:24] Carlos: sample traffic volume — for prod we'd expect spikes ~2k req/s globally but for POC we'll simulate 400 req/s embeddings, and 100 concurrent chat sessions.
[09:33] Priya: good, we'll size the POC accordingly and pick instance types for the endpoints to mimic production.
[09:40] Samir: security review — can we do a separate short session with Redwood security? not the whole team, just us and maybe Priya. pinpoint our questions on telemetry, keys, and logging.
[09:49] Priya: absolutely. Jordan, can you coordinate a 30-min security deep-dive next week?
[09:54] Jordan: yes I'll set that up. proposed slot Thu 2026-09-17 10am PT. I'll send invite after the call.
[10:02] Lena: anything else we need to decide now?
[10:05] Carlos: just confirm which VPC pattern — we'll start with peering and keep PrivateLink as backup. agree?
[10:10] Priya: yes start with peering, we can pivot if routing constraints pop up.
[10:16] Jordan: recap of next steps — Redwood shares security pack and runbook; NovaHealth shares AWS account and VPC details; schedule benchmark window; 3-week POC goal.
[10:26] Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[10:28] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[10:30] Meeting end
